chapter: Trent's band: Arkansas, Dallas and the Adolphus
title: Touring Eldorado, passing the hat and Andy Kirk's origins
summary: On tour they pass the hat for food and rooms; talk of Louis Jordan's home town and Andy Kirk getting his band from the trumpeter.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: THEN YOU GRADUATED FROM SCHOOL AND FINALLY GET OUT OF HIGH SCHOOL. THEN YOU WERE WITH HIM FULL TIME. THAT'S WHEN YOU GO DOWN TO TEXAS?
Well we made a tour down to Helena, I don't mean Helena, I mean Eldorado.
Yeah, Arkansas. That's Louie Jordan's home.
DID YOU MET HIM AROUND THAT TIME?

No, I don't remember meeting him. I don't think I knew him until later. You see that band was so outstanding that a lot of the guys who knew me, had been guys who played in the band. Andy Kirk said he met me years ago in Dalls when we did a concert. Well, I didn't remember that.
HE WASN'T ANYBODY AT THAT TIME.
No, he wasn't. You see because Andy Kirk got his band.
He got it from T----. T---- was our trumpet player.

And I getting a little ahead of my story. We played we had to pass the hat in Eldorado. That's how we would eat and that's how we got money to get our room. I'll never forget the nights we passed the hat around and we played on this corner for about 2 hours and the Cats were really playing and we got enough money to get sandwiches and to pay for a room. We would double up and that's how we lived. We didn't know anybody in the band, everybody in the

band was from families that could well-afford to give them what they wanted, but we didn't. We were determined to make it on our own. Anyway, we left there and went into Dallas. And we were playing out a place called Oak Cliff.
